@copilot Update this PR directly to fix the rpc/dup compatibility regression in its service-name change. Preserve the current main base, draft state, RPC preview flag, and generated IDL identity discovery for both synchronous and asynchronous processors. Do not open another PR or change unrelated conformance behavior.

The current getServerServiceName replaces the single request service name whenever preview is emitted, including rpc/dup. ThriftRpcAttributesGetter.getService then returns that replacement for the legacy rpc.service attribute as well as getRpcMethod using it for preview. As a result rpc/dup changes legacy rpc.service on server spans and the legacy server duration metric from the handler implementation class to the generated IDL service. The revised AbstractThriftTest assertions currently hide this by calling getServerServiceName for legacy RPC_SERVICE expectations. Copilot review 5659242123 has no findings, but this separate full-diff compatibility issue remains actionable.

Keep the legacy handler identity and logical preview IDL identity independently available through request/decorator/getter wiring. In rpc/dup, the preview span name and fully qualified rpc.method and preview duration metric method must use the generated IDL service, while the legacy rpc.service on spans and legacy server duration metrics must retain the concrete handler class. The shared rpc.method attribute can follow the existing preview-wins convention in dual mode; do not try to emit two conflicting values for that one attribute. Default legacy-only names and attributes must remain unchanged. Preview-only output must not add legacy attributes. Explicit service names passed to library wrappers must keep their existing behavior, and existing public constructors or wrapper methods must remain source-compatible if the shared request/decorator classes need an internal extension.

Update the shared assertions to distinguish preview logical identity from legacy handler identity rather than using one substituted name for both. Exercise the actual synchronous and asynchronous agent paths for original and renamed inherited handlers, including unrelated interfaces, with assertions for both legacy rpc.service and preview rpc.method in the same rpc/dup trace and for the corresponding old and preview duration metrics. Reuse the existing default, preview, and dual-emission suites; preserve library-wrapper coverage. Keep the fix focused and avoid copying service-discovery logic or adding configuration. Run the narrowest relevant spotlessApply directly before targeted behavior validation, preserving caches and reporting any actual validation blocker.

replies.body: Fixed in cfac1d59. Legacy handler identity and preview IDL identity now remain separate through both sync and async server paths; the default, preview, dual-emission, and library-wrapper suites pass.

threads.body: [General] This overload breaks source compatibility with the existing nullable-address constructor: `new ThriftRequest("method", "service", null, null, emptyMap())` previously compiled, but now ambiguously matches both five-argument constructors. This affects consumers of the published `opentelemetry-thrift-0.13` library even though current repository call sites compile. Use a named factory or the new six-argument constructor for distinct service names instead of adding this conflicting overload.

replies.body: Fixed in 8663a1c2. The conflicting five-argument overload is removed, and internal calls use the unambiguous six-argument constructor. The regression test includes the exact existing null-address call without casts and verifies both service identities and null addresses.
Removed the conflicting overload, preserved the existing constructor signatures and behavior, and added a regression test for the exact null-address call. Commit: `8663a1c2`.

@copilot Update this PR directly to fix the Java 8 CI failure in the new serviceIdentityDoesNotDependOnAsyncHandler test. Preserve its main base, draft state, all production behavior, existing service identities, public APIs, and default/preview/dual-emission coverage. Do not create another PR.

CI job https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/actions/runs/40560828308/job/122414569173?pr=20988 fails in :instrumentation:thrift-0.13:javaagent:test on Java 8. Both inherited=false and inherited=true cases time out at ThriftTest.java:121 after the Thrift async selector thread crashes with java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: java.nio.ByteBuffer.rewind()Ljava/nio/ByteBuffer; from org.apache.thrift.async.TAsyncMethodCall.doWritingRequestBody. This is the known Thrift 0.13/Java 8 async-client incompatibility, not a telemetry assertion failure.

At the beginning of serviceIdentityDoesNotDependOnAsyncHandler in instrumentation/thrift-0.13/javaagent/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/thrift/v0_13/ThriftTest.java, apply the same compatibility assumption already used by the shared async tests in instrumentation/thrift-0.13/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/thrift/v0_13/AbstractThriftTest.java: assumeTrue(!"1.8".equals(System.getProperty("java.specification.version")) || testLatestDeps());. Add the necessary existing-helper and JUnit static imports. Keep this surgical and test-only. Skip only the known Java 8/baseline-dependency combination, retaining execution on newer JDKs and compatible latest dependencies. Do not increase timeouts, alter dependencies, disable the synchronous test, or change instrumentation behavior.

Run the narrowest relevant spotlessApply directly before targeted validation. Validate both parameterized async cases on a supported JDK and, if available, verify they skip with baseline Thrift on Java 8. Preserve the existing default, preview, and rpc/dup suite wiring and assertions. Report any actual environment blocker rather than claiming validation passed.

replies.body: Added the Java 8/baseline-Thrift assumption to the async identity test. Both parameter cases pass on Java 25 and skip on Java 8. Commit: `465eedba`.

@copilot Update this PR directly to make the best-effort Thrift service-name lookup resilient to reflection and class-loading failures. Preserve successful service discovery, synchronous and asynchronous instrumentation, the existing base and draft/ready state, and explicit library-wrapper behavior. Do not create another PR.

In instrumentation/thrift-0.13/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/thrift/v0_13/ThriftSingletons.java, wrap each class's generic introspection inside serviceNames.computeValue in try/catch (Throwable t), inside the superclass loop. Cover getTypeParameters(), getBounds(), and the related bound inspection rather than enumerating exception types. Log the failure at FINE using the existing java.util.logging conventions, identifying the class being inspected, and continue checking its superclass. If no service is found, retain the existing empty-string result so ClassValue caches it and getServerServiceName falls back to the handler class name. Do not cache a handler-specific name in the processor-class cache.

The existing advice-level suppress = Throwable.class protects the application but is not sufficient here: a lookup failure currently aborts advice before the synchronous decorators are installed or the asynchronous service name is assigned. Keep the catch narrowly scoped to this optional metadata lookup so instrumentation continues with the existing fallback. Do not change telemetry identities on successful lookup, public APIs, configuration, library documentation, or unrelated code.

Add focused regression coverage for failed generic inspection, superclass continuation, and the handler fallback using existing test utilities where practical. Run the narrowest applicable spotlessApply directly before targeted behavior validation, and report any actual validation blocker.

replies.body: Added a narrowly scoped `Throwable` catch around each processor class’s generic metadata inspection, logging at `FINE` and continuing to its superclass. Added unit coverage for failed bound inspection, superclass discovery, and handler-name fallback. Commit: `35daa78d`.
